findings: HB185 explicitly calls M1584 a packing strip under angle cleats. The prior between-flange interpretation is superseded; the next candidate puts each strip between the body side cleat foot and casing sheet. Thickness and exact strip outline remain inferred.

HB185 lists M1585 beading quantity4 and separate M1586 cap beading quantity4, while SNL55/60 list two M1585 on each body and cap (eight per vehicle). HB also lists only one casing under its per-machine heading, whereas SNL lists two vehicle casings. These source quantity scopes and beading identities conflict; they are not silently merged.

SNL191:001 directly assigns five3/16x5/8inch countersunk rivets to each M1585 bead. Eight beads with five each gives40vehicle rivets, matching the SNL nested ten per body/cap. The global row1082 also allocates426+250+386 to stowage, leaving20 for beading, another global/nested conflict.
SNL147 confirms4 M1581 register plates and2each M1594A/right and M1594B/left. Profiles, locations and interlocking details are not dimensioned.

For register plates the working schedule uses four long5/16x7/8rivets per plate: bodyM1581 follows the direct joint entry; capM1594 follows its nested assembly remainder after six long side-cleat rivets. The independent cap short-rivet entry remains contradictory.

HB134 describes bolted casing support and removal by nuts at hull back plates; SNL170 explicitly identifies M2003/M1592 rivets. Existing riveted wall-collar geometry follows the named SNL joint; this tension in the sources remains open.
